summary: A granite house and tower on a gravel shoal mid-Sound, first marked by a lightship; lit 1877 or 1878, automated 1970, and offered at auction in 2023.

facts.agency: Sold at GSA auction 2023; current owner not confirmed in sources read

notes_for_editor: First-lighting year disputed (Dec 1877 vs Dec 1878); Light-House Board reports for 1878-79 are not in the corpus (lhb starts 1891) and would settle it. Roster/Bulletin conflict: Bulletin 1921 names J. A. Burk as an additional keeper on 18 Oct 1921, but the USLHS roster has Burk only from 1 Dec 1921 as second assistant; the roster line is kept as printed. 1905 incident: the New Haven Union OCR garbles names (Merrill Halse = Morrell Edson Hulse; head keeper garbled); LighthouseFriends says five days, the paper seven. Record location: NRHP lists Fairfield County on the form, the supplementary record says New Haven; official maps put it in Connecticut (LF). The 1933 Bulletin calls the station Conn., others N.Y. Bulletin 1933 OCR is garbled; quotes are short fragments. Current owner after the 2023 auction not confirmed; the stratfordshoal.org site (appears to be owner-run, copies LighthouseFriends text) was not used as a source. Roster lines (249) are all attributed to source 3 and were machine-parsed; roster has no other_stations. Hulbert listed as George P. Hulbert III in USLHS (LF prints II). No role on the 1960-70 USCG crew beyond "other".
